question: What must the prime powers of an odd perfect number look like?
answer: Euler showed that in the factorisation of an odd perfect number, exactly one prime appears to an odd exponent while all others appear to even exponents. Each σ(p^a) adds a+1 odd terms, so it is even only when a is odd. Since σ(n) = 2n holds the factor 2 just once, only one σ can be even.
move: An odd perfect number has exactly one prime raised to an odd power.
